intro.title: Build typed nav schema and guards
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed navigation schema and guard functions to safely manage routes in a TypeScript application. You'll learn how to define a set of allowed routes as a union type, creating a single source of truth for your app's navigation. Using this schema, you will implement guard functions that use type narrowing to check if a given string is a valid route before navigating. This approach ensures type safety, prevents runtime errors, and provides better developer experience through autocompletion and error checking.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building robust navigation systems in enterprise applications like admin dashboards, e-commerce platforms, and SaaS products. For example, in a banking dashboard, typed navigation schemas ensure users can only access routes appropriate to their role (customer vs. admin), while guards prevent unauthorized access to sensitive financial data pages. Developers implement these to create maintainable, type-safe navigation structures that prevent runtime errors and enforce business rules across complex multi-view applications.
